name: Child-Friendly Streets (Shanghai, children 7–12)
description: Method replication: the images are new Baidu street views of Shanghai, not the paper's stimuli. Children aged 7–12 rate how child-friendly each street looks on a five-point scale (1 worst, 2 poor, 3 average, 4 good, 5 excellent), as in the child perception survey of Tu, Miao & Jin (2026, PLOS ONE). The paper kept a street's rating only when at least 12 of 20 children gave the same score and the standard deviation was at most 0.7, and used the most frequent score. Differences from the original study: (1) children rated streets on site with an interviewer, here they rate photos online; (2) the paper's photos were taken from the sidewalk at a child's eye height (about 1.3 m), Baidu street views are taken from a car roof; (3) 20 images per child.
author: Tu, Miao & Jin
